title: Strong Converse for Quantum Capacity via a Fully Quantum Blowing-Up Lemma
abstract: We prove an exponential strong converse for quantum communication through every finite-dimensional memoryless channel: at any fixed rate above the quantum capacity, the entanglement-transmission fidelity of every code decays exponentially with the number of channel uses. The proof has two main ingredients. First, a fully quantum blowing-up lemma converts a low-fidelity code into a high-fidelity code, with a loss in the number of transmitted qubits controlled by the projective tensor norm of the orthogonal projection on the image of the Stinespring dilation of the channel across the receiver--environment bipartition. Second, a low-degree polynomial construction approximates the tensor power of this projector with exponential accuracy while controlling its projective norm, providing the approximation needed for the blowing-up argument.
summary: This paper rigorously proves an exponential strong converse for quantum capacity, showing that exceeding the channel's capacity leads to an exponentially decaying fidelity for any quantum code. The proof is highly technical, relying on a 'fully quantum blowing-up lemma' and advanced polynomial approximation techniques to control error accumulation over many channel uses.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove an exponential strong converse for quantum communication capacity through any finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channel.
main_result: It establishes that if the transmission rate exceeds the quantum capacity by any positive gap, the entanglement-transmission fidelity of the code must decay exponentially with the number of channel uses.
method: The proof combines a 'fully quantum blowing-up lemma' (to convert low-fidelity codes to high-fidelity ones) with a low-degree polynomial construction to approximate the tensor power of the channel's projection operator.
model_or_system: The model is a point-to-point quantum channel N used multiple times (memoryless channel). Communication is analyzed using entanglement-transmission codes.
key_observables: Entanglement-transmission fidelity ($F_n$), communication rate (qubits per channel use), and the quantum capacity $Q(N)$.
important_parameters: The rate gap ($\gamma > 0$) and the exponential decay constant ($\alpha_\gamma > 0$) are central parameters.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on the ability to approximate the tensor power of the projection operator using low-degree polynomials while controlling the projective tensor norm.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the entanglement transmission process through the channel N, using the Stinespring isometry.
paper_structure: The structure builds from defining the strong converse problem, introducing the fully quantum blowing-up lemma, and then using polynomial approximation techniques to control the error terms necessary for the final exponential decay bound.
why_interesting: While highly theoretical, the techniques involving projector approximation and tensor norms are mathematically sophisticated and could inspire new ways to bound error propagation in complex quantum systems or quantum network protocols.
